reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 13: SPX 7,561.67 is 3.61% off its 120-day high, 1.38% below its 50-day and 3.02% above its 200-day; SMH $486.75 is inside Zone 2 ($470-505) and 27.55% off its high; NVDA $162.85 is BELOW Zone 2 ($175-185), 33.09% off its high with RSI 24.9; VIX 19.30 and HY OAS 3.2 are calm; mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4 confirmed.
reaction.invalidation: SPX closes above the $7,750-7,820 failure zone with SMH above $580 and NVDA reclaiming $185 — the correction thesis is void and the stance flips to re-evaluating longs; or HY OAS above 4.0 with VIX above 25, which voids the calm-credit, rotation-not-rollover read entirely.

ladder.response: Stay in Watch. Do not chase the breakdown and do not bottom-fish the next zone down without a new tally print; re-check zone occupancy and tally at the next close.
ladder.trigger: SMH daily close below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA daily close below $150

ladder.response: Treat it as the trap case: no chasing the first bounce, no new entries on the bounce. Wait for the failure-zone retest verdict before any Tranche A consideration.
ladder.trigger: SMH bounces into the failure zone $580-600 or SPX into $7,750-7,820 and fails there

ladder.response: Stand down. Tranche A and Tranche B stay off, new money stays 100% bills, and the rotation read is void — the regime has broken to risk-off.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4.0 or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Tranche A re-arms: deploy 25% per the ladder into Zone 2 names (SMH/NVDA/MU zone prints), sized per the deployment ladder, not all at once.
ladder.trigger: NVDA daily close at or above $175 AND SMH holding $470 AND mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better (VIX rollover or volume climax confirms)

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the live risk: a sharp bounce into the SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820 failure zone that fails there would trap first-bounce buyers. Entries therefore wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — a bounce that holds above the failure zone changes the read, a bounce that rejects it confirms the correction and keeps the stance at Watch.

strategyPosture: Watch. The episode is a CORRECTION with the AI complex in or below its buy zones, but no capitulation signal has confirmed and Tranche A is not re-armed (tally 2 of 4, NVDA below its $175 floor). Hold bills, hold the book, let the zone levels and the tally do the work.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking because credit can flip, but nothing in the data yet says broad rollover: the index is holding its 200-day and credit is not cracking. The risk is treating a leadership rotation as a market top and de-risking the whole book on a Mag7 problem.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names sit 16.43% below their 52-week highs on average against SPY at 3.5% below its high, a 12.93-point divergence gap, and SPX itself is only 3.61% off its 120-day high (7,561.67 vs 7,844.52) while still 3.02% above its 200-day (7,340.32). Credit confirms the rotation read rather than a rollover: bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.2, calm.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a Mag7-led unwind: NVDA is 33.1% off its high and QQQ is 7.38% lower over one month while SPY is only 2.88% lower, which looks like the index leadership breaking.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.0 or SPX closing below its 200-day at 7,340.32 — either would void the rotation read and confirm rollover.

themes.counterRead: The gap between price and fundamentals is the opportunity, but it is not yet a buy: NVDA sits BELOW its Zone 2 floor ($162.85 vs the $175-185 zone), SMH is inside Zone 2 ($486.75 vs $470-505) without a capitulation print, and the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4 (no volume climax, no VIX rollover). Fundamentals ahead of price is the setup; the trigger is still missing.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals moved the other way. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year with the stock 33.1% below its high and RSI at 24.9 (oversold); AVGO revenue is up 55% with a 42.1% free-cash-flow margin; DDOG revenue is up 27.7% with an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow while 38.8% below its high; ONTO revenue is up 41.5% while 47.3% below its high. Of the 14 FULL_SIGNAL dislocations, 11 are tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN and only NVDA is ACUTE_CATALYST — the selloff is repricing sentiment, not reported demand.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure Washout
themes.narrative: The market has priced AI infrastructure as a busted trade: NVDA fell 12.75% in five days and 25.88% over one month, SMH is 27.55% off its high and below its 200-day, and the whole complex (PLTR -17.54%, AVGO -29.9% off high, LRCX -48.5% off high) is being sold as if demand broke.
themes.watchFor: NVDA daily close back at or above $175 with SMH holding $470 — the zone reclaim that re-arms Tranche A.

themes.counterRead: VST at $133.01 is below its 50-day ($145.08) and the entry is still not armed — the next leg is the 50-day reclaim, not the current price. The data says the thesis is intact; the tape says wait for the level. Buying the narrative of a power supercycle without the level is chasing.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the board's top conviction promotion (score 83): revenue is growing 19.1% year over year, free cash flow is $1,318M, P/S is 2.5x, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. BWXT is 49.1% below its high with revenue growing 18.3% and positive free cash flow of $185M. The theme's decline is tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN across the board, not a demand break.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power
themes.narrative: Nuclear and power names were sold with the AI complex: VST is 15% lower over one month and 29.7% below its high, GEV is down 14.73%, CCJ 15.57%, OKLO 22.56% and SMR 25.55% over the same month, as if the power-demand story had been repriced away.
themes.watchFor: VST daily close back above its 50-day at $145.08.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree here, which is itself the signal: this is de-leveraging, not indiscriminate selling. The names that held up are the ones with cash flow and real demand; the ones that fell are the ones that needed the story to keep running. That split is information, not noise — it says the tape is discriminating, which argues against blanket de-risking and for name-level triage.
themes.dataAnchor: The ranking of the damage is exactly what a leverage unwind looks like: the harder the leverage and the thinner the fundamental anchor, the deeper the fall — CONL -55.68% and TQQQ -23.75% against SPY -2.88% over one month. Portfolio holdings sit in the blast radius: BMNR -26.07% over one month (-6.4% Friday), DOGE -23.7%, CONL -55.68%. Meanwhile the unlevered, cash-generative leaders held up (MA +7.28% over one month, TMDX +19.42%, NXT +13.22%).
themes.label: Speculative Leverage Unwind
themes.narrative: The most-leveraged, most-narrative names fell hardest in the same tape: crypto and its proxies (BTC -19.19% in one month, ETH -22.05%, COIN -31.42%, IBIT -17.15%), leveraged single-stock ETFs (CONL -55.68%, TQQQ -23.75%) and story stocks (RDDT -38.94%, HIMS -33.93%) led the decline.
themes.watchFor: BTC-USD and CONL stabilizing after their -19.19% and -55.68% one-month slides while SPY holds its 200-day — a leverage unwind that stops spreading is the first sign the tape is finding a floor.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds at the NVDA $175 reclaim and the SMH $470 floor: SMH is already inside Zone 2 at $486.75 and NVDA is $12 below its zone floor, so the first confirmed zone reclaim plus a third tally signal is where the tape either bottoms or breaks to the next zone down.
